 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the appellant/3rd respondent in O.P (MV) No.87 of 2012 on the file of the Principal Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Kozhikode challenging the liability to pay compensation awarded by the tribunal.

entities.text: Principal Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Kozhikode
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The respondents herein are the claimants and respondents 1,2 & 4 before the tribunal.

2. According to the respondents/claimants, on 24.11.2010 at about 04.00 pm, while the deceased was walking along the extreme side of the road, a bus driven by the 2 nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit the deceased.
As a result of the accident, he sustained serious injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

The learned counsel for the respondent submitted that, pursuant to the filing of this appeal, the Tribunal, on the basis of the review petition filed by the claimant, has modified the total award amount to 1,88,000/-.

3. Heard the learned standing counsel appearing for the insurance company, the learned counsel appearing for the 10 th respondent/owner and the learned counsel appearing for the 11 th MACA NO. 550 OF 2014 2025:KER:40250 respondent/driver.
4.
The learned standing counsel appearing for the insurance company submitted that there was no valid policy at the time of the accident and the said contention was raised in the written statement.
The learned counsel also relied upon Ext.B1 true copy of the policy produced before the tribunal.

5. The learned counsel appearing for the owner also relied upon Ext.A4 policy photocopy of which was produced before the tribunal and submitted that as per Ext.A4, the policy was valid from 14.11.2010 to 13.11.2011, the date of the accident being 24.11.2010.

The tribunal has acted upon Ext.A4 photocopy of the policy and found that the policy was valid at the time of accident and awarded a total compensation of 1,25,000/- with interest at the rate of 8% to be paid by the insurer.
6. On a perusal of Exts. A4 and B1 policy documents, it is seen that as per Ext.B1, the period of coverage was shown as 14.12.2010 to 13.12.2011.

Though the tribunal has considered Ext.B1, it was found that the insurance company has not put forward any explanation as regards Exts.A4 and B1.
ISince

, in the written statement filed by the insurer, a specific contention was MACA NO. 550 OF 2014 2025:KER:40250 taken that there was no valid policy, the owner ought to have produced the original of the policy relevant at the time of accident.
He is the custodian of the original policy being the insured.
However, the owner did not care to do so, and he remained ex- parte.
However, in the appeal, the owner has entered appearance through his counsel.

At the time of hearing, the learned counsel appearing for the owner seeks for one more opportunity to prove the validity of the policy,
at the time of accident.

3 relied on Ext.B1 document.
Upon verifying Exts.A4 and B1 it is difficult to come to a conclusion as regards the validity of the policy coverage, without further evidence.
Hence the matter needs to be remanded back to the tribunal.
Accordingly, the award passed by the tribunal in O.P.(MV) No.87 of 2012 is set aside.
The tribunal is hereby directed to determine the validity of the policy as expeditiously within a period of six months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
If it is found by the tribunal that the vehicle had a valid insurance policy at the time of accident, the tribunal shall also decide on the aspect of compensation to be awarded to the claimant.
The parties MACA NO. 550 OF 2014 2025:KER:40250 are directed to appear before the tribunal on 01.07.2025.
The parties appearing on both sides will be at liberty to adduce fresh evidence to prove their case.

Sd/-
